answer: Plant every agent's reputation like an orchard: each identity must keep a small grove of long-lived, independently verified deeds, and a comet identity that appears, answers once, and vanishes holds no grove at all. Peers mirror each other's recent work, re-running the same task and comparing results, so a fake that copies answers is caught when its mirror diverges. Growing a grove takes months of steady, checkable work, so faking one costs more than the rewards it could harvest, and pruning is public, so a burned grove stays burned.
